newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down on selling of key stocks.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down on selling of key stocks.

text.p: A lack of fresh incentives plus declines on Wall Street and several regional markets forced investors to sell some key issues, causing the Thai stock market to end down in thin trade on Friday, brokers said.
"There was no new positive factor to boost investment today. Declines in Wall Street overnight and other Asian markets worsened the market mood," said a broker at a foreign brokerage house.
The SET index ended 0.61 point lower at 848.56 on about three billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 0.09 point higher at 63.82.
Decliners led advancers 171 to 113 while 98 issues were unchanged.

"Foreigners weren't active today. Also, most of the local investors stayed on the sidelines because they are awaiting for last year earnings results for other sectors after banks and finance firms released their earnings earlier this week," said the broker.
Brokers said plans by the Bank of Thailand to release key national economic data next Thursday was another factor that sidelined investors.

The banking sector gained most in terms of value, rising 0.23 percent. Several key sectors retreated including the finance sector, which dropped 0.67 percent, the energy sector fell 0.88 percent and the property sector declined 1.19 percent.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling 0.50 baht to 52. Italian-Thai Development dipped four to 134 while Electricity Generating slipped three to 68.50 and National Finance and Securities unchanged at 48.25.
